userStories.title: Re-attach jobs, poll progress and tail logs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the runner to discover existing repo jobs, poll their lifecycle/progress, tail logs and stop timers safely.

**Motivation** — That stitching is the pain the roadmap exists to remove.

**Approach** — `createJobRunner` gains `attach()` (re-attaching this repo's records, with no notices), the `JOB_POLL_MS` poll (liveness of re-attached jobs, `run` progress and cost), re-attached finalization (adopting an already-terminal record), `logTail` and `dispose()` (stopping the poll), as described under Design § Data shapes. Tests go in a new `test/unit/chat/jobs/job-runner-attach.test.ts`, with the same stubs and fake clock.

Polling uses a chained cancellable `setTimeout` of `JOB_POLL_MS` (the documented exception in the forbidden-patterns table), armed only while a job is running. Each tick: a re-attached running job whose pid is dead is finalized (see re-attached finalization below), and queues a notice when this runner wrote its terminal state; a running `run` job's `cost` and `progress` are refreshed from `readRunProgress`, and a change is emitted when either changed. Refreshed values are kept in memory and written with the final record.

`attach` reads `readJobRecords(outputDir)` and keeps the records whose `cwd` equals `repoRoot`. A `running` record whose pid is alive is tracked by polling. A `running` record whose pid is dead is finalized and written, and queues NO notice: stale jobs found at startup are visible in `list()` and `/jobs`, and must not start a stack of model turns.

Re-attached finalization: before writing a terminal state for a job it did not spawn, the runner re-reads that job's record. If the record is already terminal (its owner wrote it), the runner adopts it unchanged, writes nothing and queues no notice. Otherwise it resolves the outcome with no exit code and writes it.

`JOB_POLL_MS`, `CANCEL_GRACE_MS` and `DEFAULT_HOST_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` are named constants, not config. The host passes the real approval timeout from `config.execution.approvalTimeout`; the other two are UI cadences, deliberately not tunable. `logTail` returns the last `JOB_LOG_TAIL_LINES = 40` lines by default and `""` when the log is missing. Notices are FIFO. `dispose()` stops polling and timers; never kills a child.

**Scope** — In: replace US-005's attach/logTail/dispose placeholders and add polling/finalization. Out: cancellation and grace timers (US-007), notices delivered as model turns (US-014). Notices for stale jobs finalized at startup (`attach`); they show in `/jobs` and `nax-jobs__list` only. A compare-and-set write of a job record across two chats; when both finalize the same job in the same moment, the last write wins (the owner writes the real exit code at exit, and the other chat adopts a terminal record it finds). Detecting a recycled pid for a re-attached job's liveness; such a job stays `running` in the list until that pid exits, and only cancel is guarded (by the `run` status-file check).

**Interface** — Extend the existing `ChatJobs` implementation without changing its signatures:
```ts
/** Loads this repo's records once; idempotent. */
attach(): Promise<void>;
logTail(id: string, lines?: number): Promise<string>;
/** Stops polling and timers; never kills a child. */
dispose(): void;
```
Use `JOB_POLL_MS = 2_000`, `JOB_LOG_TAIL_LINES = 40`, the runner's timer/liveness seams and US-003's `readRunProgress` / `resolveJobOutcome`.

userStories.title: Complete job list, cancel and instruction tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the static nax-jobs provider with bounded job inspection, explicitly approved cancellation and prompt instructions.

**Motivation** — The standing rule is that a billed launch needs the user's explicit yes at the launch moment (user).

**Approach** — `createJobsProvider` gains the `list` and `cancel` tools and `instructions()` returning `buildJobsInstructions()`, as in Design § The `nax-jobs` provider. `JOBS_LIST_LIMIT` is exported from `jobs-provider.ts`. Tests go in a new `test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.test.ts`.

`list` with no `job` returns JSON `{ "jobs": [...], "omitted": <n> }`, at most `JOBS_LIST_LIMIT = 20` newest first. Each entry has `id`, `kind`, `target`, `state`, `startedAt`, and `endedAt`, `progress`, `cost`, `note` when present. `list` with `job` returns that record's fields plus `logTail`, the last `JOB_LOG_TAIL_LINES` lines of its log.

`cancel` first calls `jobs.canCancel(id)`; on `{ ok: false }` it returns `[chat] <message>` as an error result with no card (this covers a job that is not running and an unverified re-attached job). Otherwise it asks with `tool: "nax-jobs__cancel"`, summary `cancel nax <kind> <target> (<id>)`, reason `Cancelling stops the job; paid work it has done is not refunded.` On `allow` it calls `jobs.cancel(id)` and returns `cancel requested for job <id>; SIGINT sent`. On `deny` it returns the error `[chat] the user declined to cancel job <id>`.

`instructions()` returns `buildJobsInstructions()`. Both list/cancel schemas use `additionalProperties: false`, with `job: string`; list has no required properties and cancel requires `job`. Reject a `job` not matching `JOB_ID_PATTERN` with error `[chat] invalid job id <id>`; an unknown id gives `[chat] unknown job <id>`. A non-running job returns `[chat] job <id> is not running (state <state>)` without a card. An unverified re-attached job returns `[chat] job <id> was started by another chat and its pid cannot be verified; stop it from that chat or by hand` without a card. Missing logs tail as `""`. Host cancellation approval uses the same unrememberable host-card path and receives the call's abort signal.

The final provider advertises exactly `plan`, `run`, `bot_review`, `bot_fix`, `list` and `cancel`, with id `nax-jobs`, kind `static`, stages `["*"]`. Four launch descriptions still include `Billed` and `asks the user`; their existing schemas are preserved.

**Scope** — In: two new tools, 20-entry projection, job id validation, cancellation preflight/card/result and provider instructions. Out: signalling internals (US-007), host registration (US-013), /jobs and the close prompt UI (US-015). No TUI picker/log-tail view, stale-startup notices, subagent launches or ACP-server registration.

**Interface** —
```ts
export const JOBS_LIST_LIMIT = 20;
export function createJobsProvider(options: JobsProviderOptions): ToolProvider;
```
Use the existing `ChatJobs.canCancel(id)`, `cancel(id)`, `list()`, `get(id)` and `logTail(id, lines?)`; `instructions(workdir)` resolves `buildJobsInstructions()` from @/prompts.

userStories.title: Guard checkout writes and format job listings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse competing coding writes during run/plan jobs and provide the plain-text /jobs listing formatter.

**Motivation** — That stitching is the pain the roadmap exists to remove.

**Approach** — New `src/chat/jobs/job-write-guard.ts` with `GUARDED_WRITE_TOOLS` and `createJobWriteGuard`, as in Design § Write guard, and new `src/chat/jobs/jobs-listing.ts` with `formatJobsListing`, as in Design § Host and screen (`/jobs`). Tests go in a new `test/unit/chat/jobs/job-write-guard.test.ts`, with a stub `running()`, and a new `test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-listing.test.ts`.

One entry: plugin `nax-jobs`, event `before_tool`. For a call whose `name` is in `GUARDED_WRITE_TOOLS`, while `jobs.running()` holds a `plan` or `run` job whose `cwd` equals `repoRoot`, the handler returns `{ kind: "block", isError: true, content: "[nax-jobs] <name> refused: nax <kind> job <id> is running in this checkout; wait for it to end or cancel it" }`, naming the newest such job. Otherwise it returns `{ kind: "allow" }`.

Two writers. The write guard is a `before_tool` loop handler (`LoopHandlerSet`, plugin name `nax-jobs`). It returns `{ kind: "block" }` for `Write`, `Edit`, `Delete` and `GitCommit` while a `run` or `plan` job for this repo is running. No `@nathapp/nax-agent` change is needed. The host appends it to its frozen loop handler set, so chat sessions and subagent sessions both get it (US-013). The `Git` tool is read-only (`GIT_READ_VERBS`) and Bash is not blocked (design 4.5).

`formatJobsListing(jobs: readonly ChatJob[]): string` lives in `src/chat/jobs/jobs-listing.ts` and is exported from `@/chat`, like `formatAgentsListing` (barrel export is US-013). One line per job, newest first, at most 20, then `+<n> more` when there are more: `<id>  <state>  <kind> <target>`, then `  <passed>/<total>` when `progress` is set, then `  $<cost.toFixed(2)>` when `cost` is set, then `  <startedAt>`. Bot targets show as `#<pr>`. No jobs gives `(no jobs)`.

**Scope** — In: guard and formatter only. Out: appending guards to parent/subagent sessions (US-013), invoking the formatter from /jobs (US-015), footer presentation (US-014). Blocking Bash, or any tool other than Write, Edit, Delete and GitCommit, while a job holds the checkout. Do not change nax-agent or the read-only Git tool.

**Interface** —
```ts
export const GUARDED_WRITE_TOOLS: readonly string[] = ["Write", "Edit", "Delete", "GitCommit"];
export function createJobWriteGuard(jobs: Pick<ChatJobs, "running">, repoRoot: string): LoopHandlerSet;
export function formatJobsListing(jobs: readonly ChatJob[]): string;
```

userStories.title: Wire jobs into the chat host and CLI
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose the optional runner/provider/guard in the chat host, wire the same executable entry from the CLI and expose close confirmation.

**Motivation** — The user ruled on 2026-10-27 that full and guarded mode are only the Bash and coding-tool permission posture, so billed launches ask in both (Q3).

**Approach** — `src/chat/jobs/index.ts` barrels the module. `src/chat/index.ts` exports the `ChatJob`, `ChatJobs` and `HostApprovalCard` types and the `formatJobsListing` function. New `src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts` with `createHostJobs` (runner, provider, guard and `confirmClose`). `ChatHostDeps.naxEntry`, `ChatHost.jobs`, `ChatHost.confirmJobsBeforeClose`, the call to `createHostJobs`, `attach` on start and resume, `dispose` on close, and the ask controller's `approvalTimeoutMs` / `now` are added in `src/chat/chat-host.ts`, as in Design § Host and screen; `chat-host.ts` stays under 600 lines. `nax-jobs` joins `RESERVED_SERVER_IDS`. `src/cli/chat.ts` gains the `naxEntry` dep and passes it on. Host tests go in a new `test/unit/chat/chat-host-jobs.test.ts`. The CLI test goes in the existing `test/unit/cli/chat-resources.test.ts`, and the reserved-id test in the existing `test/unit/chat/chat-mcp.test.ts`.

Same nax. The child argv starts with the chat process's own entry, `naxEntry`: `[process.execPath, process.argv[1]]`, resolved once at the CLI boundary in `src/cli/chat.ts`. This is `bun <repo>/packages/nax/bin/nax.ts` for a local build and `bun .../dist/nax.js` for the global install. The child never resolves `nax` from `PATH`, which closes the version trap. When `process.argv[1]` is undefined, no `naxEntry` is passed, and the host registers no `nax-jobs` provider.

Composition. The host builds the runner, the provider and the guard itself, the way it builds `createAgentsProvider`, because the provider needs the host's ask controller and session id. The composition and the close prompt live in a new `src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts` (`createHostJobs`), so `chat-host.ts` (538 lines, held to the 600-line source limit) gains only the call sites. They exist only when the host has both `resources` and a `naxEntry`. The provider sits after the resources' own providers and before `nax-agents`. Subagent sessions do not receive it: they get `resources.toolProviders` only, so a subagent cannot launch billed work.

`createHostJobs(...)` in `src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts` returns `{ jobs, provider, guard, confirmClose }`. `createChatHost` with both `resources` and `naxEntry` calls it and so builds the runner (`createJobRunner({ repoRoot, outputDir, now })`), the provider (with `approve: (card) => this.asks.requestHostApproval(card)`, `sessionId: () => this.current().sessionId`, `maxIterations: config.execution.maxIterations` and `interactionPlugin: config.interaction?.plugin ?? "cli"`) and the guard. `toolProviders` becomes `[...resources.toolProviders, nax-jobs, nax-agents?]`. The loop handler set becomes `[...pluginHandlers, ...ruleDeliveryHandlers, ...guard]`, still frozen. `host.jobs` is the runner. Without either input, none of this exists and `host.jobs` is undefined.

`start()` and `resume()` await `jobs.attach()` after the session opens.

`confirmJobsBeforeClose()`: with no `owned()` jobs it resolves without asking. Otherwise it asks with `tool: "nax-jobs__close"`, summary `<n> nax job(s) still running: <ids comma-separated>`, reason `Yes cancels them. No keeps them running in the background; a later nax chat in this repo picks them up.` `allow` calls `jobs.cancel` for each owned job; a cancel that rejects is logged through the host logger's `warn` and the rest are still cancelled. `deny`, including a timeout, keeps them. `host.confirmJobsBeforeClose` is `confirmClose` from `createHostJobs`, and is undefined when the jobs pieces do not exist.

`close()` calls `jobs.dispose()` and never cancels a job. The SIGTERM and SIGHUP shutdown path in `runShell` calls `host.close()` directly, so it keeps running jobs without asking.

Changed integration targets:
- `ChatHostDeps` gains `readonly naxEntry?: readonly string[]`. `ChatHost` gains `readonly jobs?: ChatJobs` and `confirmJobsBeforeClose?(): Promise<void>`. The ask controller is created with `approvalTimeoutMs: config.execution.approvalTimeout` and `now: deps.now`.
- `RESERVED_SERVER_IDS` becomes `new Set(["nax-skills", "nax-agents", "nax-workflow", "nax-jobs"])`.
- `_chatCommandDeps.naxEntry: () => readonly string[] | undefined`, default `process.argv[1] === undefined ? undefined : [process.execPath, process.argv[1]]`; `composeChat` passes `naxEntry` to `createChatHost` when it is defined.

Existing host fixtures supply no naxEntry: host-subagents.test.ts keeps nax-agents last and resource providers unchanged; chat-host-resources.test.ts keeps plugin/rule-delivery event ordering. The host interfaces only gain optional jobs members. Prove composition by capturing the session open arguments, invoking the actual frozen guard, opening a launch tool from a full-mode host and observing a real pending host card, and checking chatCommand's host dependencies.

**Scope** — In: jobs module/barrel, conditional composition, host lifecycle and close-confirmation method, CLI entry capture and MCP reservation. Out: footer/notice delivery (US-014), /jobs and user-key close sequencing (US-015). Giving subagent sessions the `nax-jobs` tools; subagents cannot launch billed work. Registering the `nax-jobs` provider in the ACP server (koda); only `nax chat` gets it. Do not alter SIGTERM/SIGHUP into interactive shutdown or merge child-job cost into chat cost.

**Interface** — Additive members:
```ts

readonly naxEntry?: readonly string[];
// ChatHost
readonly jobs?: ChatJobs;
confirmJobsBeforeClose?(): Promise<void>;
```
`createHostJobs(...)` returns `{ jobs, provider, guard, confirmClose }`; `HostApprovalCard` is exported from ask-controller and re-exported from @/chat with ChatJob, ChatJobs and formatJobsListing.

userStories.title: Show running jobs and deliver end notices while idle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the footer job strip and reliable FIFO job-notice turns to the chat screen.

**Motivation** — That stitching is the pain the roadmap exists to remove.

**Approach** — `formatJobStrip`, `FooterJob` and the `footerModel` `jobs` input in `src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts`; the new hook `src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts`; and the `ChatApp` wiring of the strip and notice delivery, as in Design § Host and screen. Strip tests go in the existing `test/unit/tui/chat/chat-status.test.ts`. Screen tests go in a new `test/ui/chat/chat-jobs.test.tsx`, using a fake `ChatHost` whose `jobs` is a stub `ChatJobs`.

`formatJobStrip(jobs: readonly FooterJob[]): string`, with `FooterJob = { kind, target, progress?, cost? }`, in `chat-status.ts`. One part per job: `run <f>` plus ` <passed>/<total>` when `progress` is set, plus ` $<cost.toFixed(2)>` when `cost` is set; `plan <f>`; `bot_review #<pr>`; `bot_fix #<pr>`. A feature name longer than 16 characters is cut to its first 15 characters plus `…`, so the strip fits the one-row footer. It shows at most two parts joined with ` · `, then ` +<n>` for the rest.

`footerModel` input gains `jobs?: readonly FooterJob[]`; when it holds at least one job, the right line starts with one span whose text is `formatJobStrip(jobs)`, followed by the existing spans. Its existing input is `{ state, status, hint, copiedChars?, glyphs? }`; empty or omitted jobs preserve existing output.

New hook `useJobs(host, { idle, deliver })` in `src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts`. It returns `host.jobs?.running() ?? []` and re-renders on `host.jobs.onChange`. Whenever `idle` is true and `peekNotice()` returns a notice, it calls `deliver(notice)`, which returns `Promise<boolean>`; only on `true` does it call `takeNotice()`. A notice is therefore never lost to a turn that did not start. `deliver` is read through a ref, so the latest `sendTurn` closure is used. At most one delivery is in flight at a time.

`ChatApp` passes `idle = !turnRunning && ask === undefined && picker.model === undefined && keys.canControl()`, `deliver` = a function that returns `false` when `sending.current` is already true and otherwise awaits `sendTurn(text)` and returns `true`, and the running jobs to `footerModel` as `jobs`.

A notice is peeked but the turn cannot start (a turn is already sending): `deliver` returns `false`; the notice stays queued for the next idle moment. Model-facing notice text remains in US-004's workflow builders, not new prompt literals in the hook. Existing footer tests continue to use the optional input without changes.

**Scope** — In: pure strip/footer additions, hook subscription and delivery coordination, real ChatApp integration. Out: runner queue construction (US-005), /jobs and close-confirmation key sequencing (US-015). A job picker or a log-tail view in the TUI; `/jobs` prints a plain listing, and the model reads a job's log through `nax-jobs__list`. A job card in the transcript (design 4.8); the launch tool's result and the end notice are the transcript record. Adding job cost to the chat session's `costUsd`; the two ledgers stay separate.

**Interface** — `formatJobStrip(jobs: readonly FooterJob[]): string`; `FooterJob = { kind, target, progress?, cost? }`; `footerModel` gains `jobs?: readonly FooterJob[]`; `useJobs(host, { idle, deliver })` returns the current running job array, with `deliver(notice): Promise<boolean>`. Reuse `ChatJobs.running`, `onChange`, `peekNotice` and `takeNotice`.

**Motivation** — Closing the chat with a running job asks whether to cancel it or keep it running in the background (Q4).

**Approach** — The `/jobs` built-in in `src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`, and the `confirmJobsBeforeClose` call in `useChatKeys.close()`, as in Design § Host and screen and § Changed (`useChatKeys.ts`). Slash command tests go in the existing `test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx`. Close tests go in a new `test/ui/chat/chat-jobs-close.test.tsx`.

`/jobs` is a new built-in slash command, placed after `agents` and before `quit` in `COMMANDS`, with description `List nax jobs`. It shows `formatJobsListing(host.jobs?.list() ?? [])`, or `jobs are not available in this session` when `host.jobs` is undefined. It makes no model call.

`src/tui/chat/useChatKeys.ts` `close()`. Baseline: sets `closing` and `locked` synchronously, then awaits `host.close()` inside a `try`. Target: when `host.confirmJobsBeforeClose` is defined, `close()` first sets a `confirming` ref and awaits it, leaving `closing` and `locked` untouched until it settles, because the ask card is only answerable while `!keys.locked` (`ChatApp.tsx:603`). A second ctrl+c or `/quit` while `confirming` is set returns at once and raises no second card. After it resolves, `confirming` is cleared and the existing closing sequence runs. When the method is absent, `close()` runs exactly as today, with no extra await, so the existing synchronous teardown path is unchanged. If the call rejects, the error is shown through `onError`, `confirming` is cleared and the chat stays open.

`useChatKeys` `close()` is the only path from `/quit` and ctrl+c to `host.close()`. `keys.canControl()` is the guard every control path shares. Do not lock the card while confirming or duplicate it on a repeated quit gesture. US-013 owns the close card itself: owned jobs only, Yes cancels, No/timeout keeps, per-job cancellation rejection logs warn and continues. SIGTERM/SIGHUP still call host.close directly.

Existing test modification: `test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx` test `US-011 AC-15 US-024 AC-15 help lists /agents between /mcp and /quit` expects the help frame to contain the three rows mcp, agents, quit back to back (List MCP servers, List agents, Quit nax chat). The new jobs built-in now sits between agents and quit, so the expected text gains the row `/jobs  List nax jobs` between the agents row and the quit row (built-ins listed in COMMANDS order, quit last, is the invariant kept).

**Scope** — In: built-in registration/listing, help-order expectation, close key sequencing and real AskCard interaction. Out: close card composition/cancel policy (US-013), listing formatting (US-012), footer and completion notices (US-014). Running `/jobs` while a turn is in flight; like every other built-in it is refused with the busy notice, and the footer strip shows running jobs meanwhile. No picker/log view or interactive SIGTERM/SIGHUP shutdown.

**Interface** — Reuse `host.jobs?: ChatJobs`, `formatJobsListing(jobs: readonly ChatJob[]): string` and `host.confirmJobsBeforeClose?(): Promise<void>`. Preserve the existing `useChatKeys.close(): Promise<void>` and `canControl(): boolean` surfaces; add the internal confirming ref, not a mandatory new host method.

analysis:
Enhancement to the existing Bun/TypeScript nax chat, not a greenfield application. All 15 binding stories run in packages/nax; nax-agent, nax-agent-acp and nax-ai are read-only dependencies. Graph-first navigation was unavailable because this session exposes no codebase-memory tools, so findings were verified with direct reads and text searches rooted at the supplied execution repository. No implementation or tests were run during PRD drafting.

Existing architecture and integration: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:55 defines ChatHost, :78 defines ChatHostDeps, :99 begins NativeChatHost, and :128-177 composes project output paths, frozen loop handlers, asks, subagents and providers. The file currently has 538 lines; use the new jobs/jobs-host.ts composition helper to remain below 600 rather than embedding job machinery in the host. The output directory already comes from getProjectKey and projectOutputDir (:135-136); packages/nax/src/runtime/paths.ts:19-32 handles the global default and absolute/tilde overrides. Store job artifacts there, not in the repo's feature tree. The host currently freezes plugin handlers followed by rule delivery (:138-146), constructs asks afterward (:147-153), passes resources.toolProviders and the shared handler set to subagents (:157-170), and conditionally appends nax-agents to parent providers (:171-173). Reorder composition carefully: asks and host jobs must exist before freezing the augmented handler set and constructing subagent runs. Parent providers must be resources, then nax-jobs, then nax-agents if present. Subagents must continue receiving resources.toolProviders only, but receive the augmented frozen guard handler set; packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-runs.ts:181-182 forwards these inputs. No change to nax-agent's tool loop is necessary.

Lifecycle: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:247-267 opens start sessions and replaces their handle; :281-284 resets asks and applies mode; :330-367 resumes sessions; :495-527 makes close idempotent, drains active opens and subagents, releases handles, tears down resources and destroys the interaction chain. Attach job records after the session opens on start and resume; attachment is idempotent across clear/resume. Dispose runner timers on close, without cancelling jobs or putting them in subagent cleanup. Session ids for launch records must come from a closure reading current(), not a captured old handle. Keep session-operation draining and late-open cleanup intact. Jobs are optional and exist only with BOTH resources and naxEntry, preserving older host fixtures and no-entry sessions.

Approval boundary: packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:8-23 declares options and interface, :43-64 handles session asks, :53 auto-allows full-mode session approvals, :71-83 controls approval memory and resolution, and :96-102 resets asks. Billed dispatch must not use handle() as its launch authority: add an independent host approval promise path, synthesized pending events, host- ids, no memory and no full-mode bypass. Host resolution must never call options.answer (which targets an AgentSession). Timeout, abort and reset all deny and remove pending events, clear timers/listeners and notify consumers. Existing session approval behavior stays unchanged. packages/nax/src/chat/ask-fallback.ts:58-84 prompts the interaction chain and resolves via the controller; :86-113 subscribes to pending asks and cleans up offers. The new events can use this fallback unchanged. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ask-card.ts:162-188 already omits the session option when canRemember is false, and packages/nax/src/tui/chat/AskCard.tsx:387-429 resolves numeric/shortcut choices through the controller. This is access-control work and requires strict three-session-tdd even where the patch is small.

Resolve [process.execPath, process.argv[1]] at this boundary once, omit naxEntry entirely when argv[1] is undefined, and never find another nax on PATH. packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts:136-172 owns shell lifetime; SIGTERM/SIGHUP must retain the existing direct host.close() path without a close card. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mcp.ts:27 reserves built-in ids and :63-69 formats collision diagnostics; reserve nax-jobs before accepting MCP providers. packages/nax/src/chat/workflow/workflow-provider.ts:80-97 is the existing static-provider pattern, and packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-types.ts:20-56 specifies Promise-returning tools(), run(input, ctx) and optional instructions(). New jobs architecture: add typed immutable records and atomic temp/rename storage, pure parsing/argv, record-authoritative outcomes, a detached-process runner, launch/provider presentation, a write guard and plain listing. No jobs module exists yet. Start/exit ownership and attachment/polling/cancellation are deliberately incremental stories US-005 through US-007; US-005's placeholders are temporary, not final behavior. US-009's four tools/no instructions and unhandled loadPRD rejection are similarly intermediate; US-010 maps failures/adds busy checks and US-011 completes six tools/instructions. The binding dependencies must not be strengthened, merged or reordered into different story ids. US-004 builds prompt helpers independently; US-011 consumes the already-created builder through upstream runner dependencies. New prompt text belongs in packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts:7-14 and its existing barrel export at packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts:132; buildWorkflowInstructions itself is unchanged. packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7-9 re-exports the shared NaxError; new thrown job errors use stage chat and CHAT_JOB_SPAWN_FAILED, CHAT_JOB_NOT_RUNNING or CHAT_JOB_UNVERIFIED as appropriate, with cause chaining rather than raw Error throws. Expose external calls via the specified _deps seams.

Concurrency and persistence risks: create the log directory, open one append fd for BOTH stdout and stderr, close it in the parent after spawn and unref the detached child. Two separately opened Bun.file log streams can overwrite one another. Register a spawned job in memory immediately after spawn returns before any further await. A launch allowed after a long card must reread the checkout lock and then check in-memory jobs immediately before invoking start, with no await between that last check and start. Pre-spawn directory creation must not introduce an unreserved asynchronous gap that lets two approved plan/run calls both pass before either spawned child is registered. Preserve the specified synchronous job visibility and existing start signature rather than inventing a new public launch API or changing binding dependencies. Disk-write failure after successful spawn must not erase knowledge of a live child. Owner exit always writes using the observed exit code. Re-attached finalizers reread the record, adopt terminal owner results unchanged, and otherwise infer without an exit code. Live pid is liveness only, not identity: cancellation of re-attached jobs is restricted to runs with a matching status pid, and bot/plan liveness cannot be strengthened in this feature. Startup stale finalization must not queue notices; later poll finalization queues only when this runner writes the result. Timer chains arm only while running, are cancellable and must not rearm after dispose. Cancel persists the intent before SIGINT, ignores dead-pid signalling failure and schedules SIGTERM only while this chat remains alive. Job cost is not chat cost.

Detecting a recycled pid for a re-attached job's liveness; such a job stays `running` in the list until that pid exits, and only cancel is guarded (by the `run` status-file check).

A compare-and-set write of a job record across two chats; when both finalize the same job in the same moment, the last write wins (the owner writes the real exit code at exit, and the other chat adopts a terminal record it finds).

Giving subagent sessions the `nax-jobs` tools; subagents cannot launch billed work.
Blocking Bash, or any tool other than Write, Edit, Delete and GitCommit, while a job holds the checkout.

Sending SIGTERM after the cancel grace period when the chat has already exited; the SIGINT is sent, and the grace timer dies with the chat.
